glance: Mercedes-Benz has stopped new investment in its German plants and says two sites could close unless labour costs fall, while EU leaders held their first AI summit in Dublin and backed seven AI gigafactories. Anthropic's IPO is reported to be heavily oversubscribed, LangChain raised 300 million dollars for agent governance, and Siemens posted a record year built on industrial AI. Also: a BMW park-outside warning, a robotaxi plan on the VW ID. Buzz, and two new papers on ultrasonic inspection and bearing vibration.
brief:
This is Vertical News for Saturday, the fourteenth of November.

Our top story: Mercedes-Benz has stopped new investment in its German plants after labour cost talks stalled, and says two German sites could close. It says production labour in Germany can cost up to five times as much as in Eastern Europe. Unions reject any closures.

In Dublin, EU leaders held their first summit on artificial intelligence. Ursula von der Leyen said Europe plans seven AI gigafactories, with about thirty billion euros for compute, and that wider tech sovereignty needs at least five hundred billion.

Anthropic's share offering is reported to be about six times oversubscribed, with pricing expected on Wednesday. LangChain raised three hundred million dollars to sell tools that govern AI agents. Notion confirmed that some AI chat transcripts were exposed through a breach at its vendor Fireworks AI. IBM previewed models that keep instructions and data apart to resist prompt injection, and Figma added native 3D transforms.

Siemens posted a record year and raised its targets on industrial AI. Applied Intuition is reportedly in talks to raise money at a thirty billion dollar valuation, and Tristar AI raised twelve point four million dollars for AI visual inspection.

May Mobility plans more than ten thousand robotaxis based on the VW ID. Buzz, and US regulators told owners of over seven hundred thousand BMWs to park outside after an earlier fix failed.

In research, Bristol engineers built a non-contact ultrasonic array that turns troublesome echoes into defect signals, and a Chinese team linked raceway waviness directly to bearing vibration.

stories.headline: Mercedes-Benz halts new investment in its German plants and says two sites could close
stories.why: Germany's premium car base is now openly up for negotiation, which affects supplier volumes, engineering jobs and where future models are developed and built.
body: Mercedes-Benz has stopped all further investment in its German sites after talks with the works council and IG Metall on cutting labour costs stalled, according to an internal memo reported by Reuters and dpa. Management wants to end the 35-hour week without full wage compensation. Production chief Michael Schiebe has warned that two German plants could close if costs do not come down far enough, though the company says its aim is still to keep every site.

Mercedes says an hour of production labour in Germany can cost up to five times as much as at its Eastern European plants. CEO Ola Källenius has said cheaper sites with longer working hours will shape where future products and investment go. The group employs about 164,000 people, roughly 108,000 of them in Germany, where job security runs to 2034 but does not guarantee products or capacity use. Third-quarter car sales fell 8% and China sales fell 31%.

Works council chief Ergun Lümali and IG Metall reject closures. For suppliers to German powertrain and assembly plants, the risk is that the next model generation, and its tooling and validation work, moves east.

stories.headline: EU leaders hold their first AI summit and back seven AI gigafactories
stories.why: EU money for compute and a lean towards European suppliers in public AI contracts will shape which AI services European product and engineering teams can use.
body: EU heads of government met informally in Dublin on Friday, hosted by Taoiseach Micheál Martin, for their first in-depth discussion of artificial intelligence. Mistral CEO Arthur Mensch joined a session on competitiveness and sovereignty, and Geoffrey Hinton a session on AI's impact on society. Because the meeting was informal, no conclusions were adopted, and a dispute over a Ukraine envoy took up much of the attention.

Council President António Costa called for faster AI adoption, fewer critical dependencies and more public and private investment, and said the proposed European Competitiveness Fund in the next long-term budget will be decisive. Commission President Ursula von der Leyen said Europe plans seven AI gigafactories, with about €30 billion expected for AI compute, and estimated that wider tech sovereignty needs at least €500 billion. She will bring a financing proposal to the next meeting. Euronews reports the EU is moving towards reserving public contracts for sensitive AI uses for European firms.
France and the Netherlands host European tech leaders in Paris on 2 December, and leaders return to AI governance in February 2027.

stories.headline: Anthropic's IPO is reported to be about six times oversubscribed ahead of pricing
stories.why: Investor demand for the largest AI listing so far will set the tone for how markets value the labs whose pricing and roadmaps shape AI products.
body: Orders for Anthropic's share offering reached roughly twice the shares available after the first day of the roadshow and about six times by the third day, Unite.ai reports, citing Reuters. The roadshow opened on 10 November. Anthropic is offering 825 million Class A shares at 70 to 78 dollars each, which would raise about 64 billion dollars at the top of the range, and underwriters may get an option on up to 123.75 million more shares.

Banks are reportedly valuing the company against projected 2028 revenue of about 270 to 280 billion dollars. Pricing is expected on 18 November and trading on Nasdaq under the ticker ANT from 19 November. Some commentators expect pricing above the range, but no decision has been announced and the SEC registration was not yet effective at the time of reporting.

For teams building on Claude, a listed Anthropic will report quarterly, giving clearer signals on capacity, pricing and product focus. The demand figures come from sources cited by Reuters, not from the company.

stories.headline: LangChain raises 300 million dollars at a 3 billion dollar valuation to sell agent governance
stories.why: Money is flowing to the layer that controls, budgets and audits AI agents, which teams need before agents go into production.
body: LangChain has raised a 300 million dollar Series C led by CapitalG, with GIC, DFJ Growth, IVP and Sapphire Ventures taking part. The 3 billion dollar valuation is more than double the 1.25 billion dollars of its previous round about a year ago.

The company started in 2022 as an open-source framework for connecting language models to search, APIs and databases. Its business now centres on LangSmith, a platform for building, running and governing agents that is not tied to any model or cloud. LangChain claims more than 7,000 LangSmith customer organisations, including Harvey, Rippling, NVIDIA, Toyota and Salesforce. New agent governance features centralise control over which models, tools and data agents can use, with gateways that set model budgets and fallbacks, protect sensitive data and manage tool access. No revenue figures were disclosed.

For product managers, the round confirms that observability, cost control and permissions are becoming separate products. Teams planning agent features should budget for this layer instead of treating it as an afterthought.

stories.headline: Notion AI chat transcripts exposed through a breach at inference provider Fireworks AI
stories.why: Every AI feature that sends user data to a model vendor inherits that vendor's security, and a zero-retention promise is not a guarantee.
body: Notion has confirmed that attackers who breached Fireworks AI, a platform that hosts open-weight models, obtained chat transcripts from Notion AI users. Notion used Fireworks for open-weight inference and for classifying conversations behind its admin feature Insights. It found that Fireworks had kept data from those endpoints despite a contractual zero-data-retention commitment. Fewer than 1% of workspaces are affected, and most transcripts cannot be tied to a user or workspace.

Notion cut its connection to Fireworks on 3 November, disabled Insights, stopped serving open-weight models through the vendor, added an incident review export in affected workspaces and told users to rotate any credentials pasted into AI chats. Its latest update, on 12 November, says third-party API keys found in messages were reported to their issuers. According to eSecurity Planet, this is Fireworks' second breach since early October.

The lesson for product teams is practical: map every subprocessor that sees prompts and outputs, check retention claims rather than trusting contracts alone, and warn users not to paste secrets into AI chats.

stories.headline: IBM previews Granite models that separate instructions from data to resist prompt injection
stories.why: Teams building agents that read emails, documents or web pages get a structural defence against hijacking, not just careful prompt wording.
body: IBM's Granite team has released two experimental Granite 4.1 models that use LLMON, a new markup for model input. Instead of ordinary characters, LLMON uses reserved special tokens to mark which parts of a prompt are instructions, which are data and which are requirements. The idea is that text inside a document or tool result is treated as material to work on, not as a command to follow. It adds to existing chat templates rather than replacing them.

IBM reports that on the OPI benchmark for indirect prompt injection, the models avoid 47% more attacks than the best frontier model it tested and 95% more than the best open model, with similar trends on two other benchmarks. General performance is said to match the standard Granite 4.1 Instruct models. The weights and a toolkit are public.

IBM is clear about the limits: these are previews, not for production, the separation is learned behaviour rather than a guarantee, and adaptive multi-turn attacks are not yet handled. All results are vendor-reported.

stories.headline: Figma adds native 3D transforms that work with its agent, Motion and code handoff
stories.why: One of designers' longest-standing Figma requests now flows through to animation and production code in a single workflow.
stories.source: AI UX Design Guide · Creators Toolbox
body: Figma has shipped native 3D transforms. Designers can rotate layers on the x, y and z axes using handles on the canvas with live previews, and adjust perspective and depth to build simple 3D scenes. Scenes can be built by hand or assembled by the Figma agent, which became generally available in October and runs on AI credits.

The feature works with Figma Motion, now in open beta with Lottie export, so designers can animate flips, turns and perspective shifts. For handoff, developers can copy the CSS from Dev Mode or send the design to a coding agent through Figma's MCP server. Figma has also published a community playground file for trying the feature. Plan and pricing details were not given in the coverage.

For product and frontend teams, the notable part is the chain from canvas to motion to code. Since browsers already support CSS 3D transforms, designs made this way should translate more directly into production than mock-ups made in separate 3D tools. This summary relies on secondary coverage of Figma's release note.

stories.headline: Siemens posts record year and raises growth targets on industrial AI
stories.why: The owner of Simcenter, Altair and Teamcenter is betting its growth on AI-driven engineering software, which will shape the CAE and PLM tools OEMs rely on.
body: Siemens reported record results for fiscal 2026. Comparable revenue rose 8% to 83.4 billion euros, orders rose 25% to 108.2 billion euros and the order backlog reached a record 143 billion euros. Digital business revenue grew 16% to 10.9 billion euros, and Digital Industries software revenue reached 7.2 billion euros, up 13% on a comparable basis. CEO Roland Busch described industrial AI as an exceptional growth opportunity.

In the fourth quarter, the Digital Industries margin rose to 20.9%. Siemens raised its mid-term revenue growth target to 7–11% from 6–9% and still aims to double digital revenue by fiscal 2030. Its investor slides cite an industrial customer reporting engineering twice as fast with Siemens' engineering agent and say revenue synergies from the Altair and Dotmatics acquisitions are starting, without giving figures.

For simulation and test engineers, the signal is that Siemens will keep pushing AI agents and Altair's solvers deeper into Simcenter and Teamcenter. Expect AI features to become a bigger part of licence negotiations.

stories.headline: Applied Intuition reportedly in talks to raise 1.5 billion dollars at a 30 billion dollar valuation
stories.why: Investors are valuing a simulation-first ADAS and vehicle software toolchain far above traditional test-tool makers, which raises the stakes for virtual validation.
body: Applied Intuition, which makes simulation and testing tools for driver assistance and automated driving as well as vehicle software, is in talks to raise at least 1.5 billion dollars, Bloomberg reports. General Catalyst would lead with about 250 million dollars. The valuation would be about 30 billion dollars, double the 15 billion dollars of its June 2025 round. No deal has been announced.

According to Tech Times, the company's revenue target for 2026 is above 560 million dollars, about 19% higher than the previous year, with forecasts of more than 1 billion dollars in 2027. That puts the reported valuation at about 54 times this year's revenue target. Applied Intuition says it works with 18 of the top 20 carmakers, and its recent deals include a vehicle operating system for trucks from TRATON, the group that owns Scania.

For validation teams, the round would fund more simulation-based sign-off tools competing with dSPACE, IPG, AVL and others. It also shows that investors see virtual testing as core vehicle software, not a niche.

stories.headline: Tristar AI raises 12.4 million dollars for AI visual inspection on existing production lines
stories.why: AI defect detection that sits on top of a plant's current cameras and control systems is reaching automotive suppliers with concrete payback claims.
body: Tristar AI, based in Cambridge, Massachusetts, has raised a 12.4 million dollar Series A led by Isogon Ventures, with investors including Capgemini's venture fund. The company sells AI-based visual quality inspection for production lines.

Tristar says its system runs on more than 500 lines in North America and Europe and connects to existing cameras, PLCs and manufacturing systems instead of replacing them. It reports defect detection accuracy of 95 to 99% in live use and a typical payback of about four months, and says it grew more than fourfold last year. Customers include suppliers to Toyota, Honda and Mercedes, as well as packaging and film makers such as Amcor and DuPont. The money will expand its vision and edge platform into new sectors.

This is optical surface inspection, not volumetric NDT, but it is where many component plants start with AI. The accuracy and payback figures are company claims; quality teams should ask for false-call rates and results on their own parts.

stories.headline: May Mobility plans more than 10,000 robotaxis based on the VW ID. Buzz by 2031
stories.why: A volume plan for driverless vans on a European production vehicle shows autonomy moving from pilots to OEM platforms and fleet-scale validation.
body: US autonomous driving company May Mobility plans to put more than 10,000 self-driving Volkswagen ID. Buzz vans into robotaxi service worldwide by the end of 2031. Volkswagen will adapt the vehicle, ECARX will supply May Mobility's autonomous driving kit, and German firm Charlton Intelligence will support delivery and deployment. The partners aim to cut the total cost per vehicle by more than half.

Public road tests in the US are planned for early 2027, with production-ready vehicles going to outside fleet operators from 2028. May Mobility does not run fleets itself; it sells its driving system to operators and ride-hail platforms, including Lyft in Atlanta. Its software runs entirely on the vehicle without needing a mobile connection and uses a world model that predicts traffic up to ten seconds ahead. The company reports more than 600,000 driverless trips and 1.1 million miles in the US and Japan.
For engineers, the plan shifts attention to vehicle-level integration, redundancy and the cost of sensors and compute at scale.

stories.headline: NHTSA tells owners of 720,796 BMWs to park outside after an earlier water-pump fix failed
stories.why: A field remedy that did not work is a clear lesson in validating connector sealing on thermal-management parts.
body: The US road safety regulator NHTSA has issued a park-outside warning for 720,796 BMW vehicles from model years 2012 to 2018, including 3, 4 and 5 Series cars, the X1, X3, X4, Z4 and 2 Series. An improperly sealed electrical connector on the electric water pump can let in water and short-circuit, which can start a fire even when the car is parked and switched off.

These vehicles were already repaired under a 2024 recall, and all of the roughly ten known US incidents happened in cars that had received that earlier fix. No crashes or injuries have been reported. A new remedy is not yet available, and owner letters go out from 25 December.

For engineers, the case shows how a first remedy can pass internal checks and still fail in the field. Environmental sealing of connectors on pumps, fans and other thermal-management components deserves the same test rigour as the parts themselves, especially as electric drivetrains add more of them.

stories.headline: Bristol researchers turn troublesome echoes into a non-contact ultrasonic array for finding defects
stories.why: A non-contact receiver that uses geometry echoes instead of fighting them could help inspect curved drivetrain parts such as rings, shafts and gear roots.
body: In conventional ultrasonic array testing, sound bouncing between a defect and a part's surfaces creates noise and false indications. A team from the University of Bristol's School of Electrical, Electronic and Mechanical Engineering uses that scattering instead. A piezoelectric probe on an angled wedge sends sound in, and a laser interferometer records the surface response at chosen points without touching the part. Those points act as a virtual phased array, and the recordings are converted into a standard full-matrix dataset and imaged in the usual way.

Tested on an aluminium block with side-drilled holes, the wedge angle controlled which directions were covered, and a large-angle wedge improved image signal-to-noise by more than 5 dB. The paper is peer-reviewed and was published online on 12 November.

This is a lab demonstration on aluminium and drilled holes, not yet on steel bearing parts or real cracks. But a flexible, non-contact array could ease inspection of curved or hard-to-couple components where standard probes struggle.

stories.headline: Study links raceway waviness directly to ball bearing vibration, validated on a production bearing
stories.why: A validated way to turn a noise target into a waviness tolerance and finishing choice is useful for low-noise e-axle bearings as well as aerospace ones.
stories.source: Lubricants (Tianjin University · Luoyang Bearing Science and Technology)
body: Researchers from Tianjin University, Luoyang Bearing Science and Technology and partner institutions built a model that links raceway waviness to the contact between balls and raceway and to the resulting vibration of angular contact ball bearings. They ranked four factors and found waviness amplitude matters most, far more than ball diameter, followed by waviness order, with every effect growing with speed. Raising amplitude from 1 to 6 micrometres lifted peak vibration from about 54 to 76 dB.

They checked the model on a production 7008 precision bearing at 1,800 rpm through four finishing stages, from coarse grinding to polishing. Measured waviness fell from 0.284 to 0.011 micrometres and vibration from 55.9 to 25.0 dB, with predictions within 1 to 4% of measurements at each stage. The paper is peer-reviewed and open access in Lubricants.
In practice, the method gives bearing engineers a way to set waviness tolerances from an NVH target. It does not report grinding settings, so translating it to a specific process still needs work.

watch.text: The IPO is expected to price on 18 November, with Nasdaq trading under ANT from 19 November.

watch.title: German labour talks
watch.text: Mercedes and IG Metall are still negotiating, and Volkswagen's restructuring talks with the union start on 24 November.
